title: Task-management Web application
source_request: Build a small local Web application for managing personal tasks.
requirements: Expose an ASGI application as app.main:app and use TASK_MANAGER_DATABASE_PATH when it is set.

Treat title as required and description, due_date, status, and priority as optional task fields. Accept todo, in_progress, and done statuses and low, medium, and high priorities; default omitted status and priority to todo and medium.
Serve the task list at GET /, accept standard HTML form submissions at POST /tasks, and expose the created task's canonical /tasks/{id} detail URL through a redirect or response link.
Serve task details at GET /tasks/{id}, edit forms at GET /tasks/{id}/edit, and standard HTML form updates at POST /tasks/{id}/edit.
Serve an explicit deletion confirmation at GET /tasks/{id}/delete and delete only after POST /tasks/{id}/delete.
Support status and priority filters on GET / with the status and priority query parameters.
Persist tasks in SQLite across application process restarts.
Preserve valid submitted values and show a useful message when form input is invalid.
Return a user-visible HTTP 404 response for missing task identifiers.
Provide automated pytest coverage and a README with installation, startup, test, and limitation instructions.
Use semantic server-rendered HTML that supports the core workflow with a keyboard alone.

acceptance_criteria.description: The documented ASGI application starts from a clean checkout and initializes its database automatically.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run CHECK_ACCEPTANCE and CHECK_PROJECT_TESTS in the fixed benchmark image.

acceptance_criteria.description: A user can create a task with all supported fields, list it, and inspect its details.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run the fixed create, list, and detail HTTP acceptance flow.

acceptance_criteria.description: A user can edit every task field and delete a task only after an explicit confirmation step.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run the fixed edit and confirmed-delete HTTP acceptance flow.

acceptance_criteria.description: The task list can be filtered by status and priority.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run the fixed status-and-priority filter acceptance flow.

acceptance_criteria.description: Tasks remain available after the application process restarts.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Create a task, restart the ASGI server with the same SQLite path, and retrieve it again.

acceptance_criteria.description: Invalid input produces a useful message without losing valid submitted values.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Submit an empty title with a valid description and inspect the returned HTML.

acceptance_criteria.description: Missing task identifiers produce a user-visible HTTP 404 response.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Request a known-missing task identifier through the fixed acceptance flow.

acceptance_criteria.description: Generated pytest tests, static compilation checks, and the fixed acceptance suite pass.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run every command in the frozen task-manager policy.

acceptance_criteria.description: The README explains installation, startup, tests, and known limitations without machine-specific paths.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run the fixed repository-structure check and independent review.

acceptance_criteria.description: Core pages use semantic HTML, associated labels, and native keyboard-operable controls.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run the fixed HTML checks and complete the human accessibility rubric.

constraints: Use Python 3.12, FastAPI, Jinja2, SQLite, and pytest.
Do not require a hosted service, external database, frontend build service, credentials, or network access at runtime.
Do not change the fixed route and environment-variable contract used by the acceptance suite.
Keep all source, tests, templates, static files, and documentation inside the supplied Git repository.
assumptions: The benchmark targets one local user and does not require authentication.
The fixed quality-gate image already contains the required Python packages.
